back: A party held to celebrate moving into a new house or flat [1].
A party to celebrate the publication of a new book or the release of a new product [1].
A 'stag party' is for a future husband and his male friends; a 'hen party' is for a future bride and her female friends before a wedding [1].
Formal parties where men are required to wear black or white bow ties, respectively [1].
The process of making useful contacts that can benefit one's business or career [1].

front: old school tie / old boy network
back: In England, refers to contacts made by children of the traditional ruling class at elite private schools [1].
To be friendly with important or famous people; often used with negative associations [1].
An informal expression meaning to mix socially with famous people [1].
A person who loves going to parties [1].
Someone who ruins a party by being disapproving, miserable, or boring [1].
A disapproving term for a small group of people who spend time together and do not allow others to join them [1].
A colloquial term for two people who are in a romantic relationship [1].
When a person fails to turn up for a planned date [1].
Staying as a guest for longer than the host would like [1].
Spending an evening visiting and having drinks in several different pubs [1].
